Sales Data Model & Semantics

This guide explains how to interpret the purchase and line-item data returned by GET /api/v1/purchases, so an accounting, inventory, or BI integration reads the numbers the same way Karma does. It complements the field descriptions on the endpoint itself.

The shape

A purchase is one payment. It has a status, an amount (total, in cents), a currency, timestamps, and a list of line items. Each line item is one thing on the receipt — a product, a tip, or an amount paid toward a split bill.

All money is in integer minor units (öre/cents), and all prices are VAT-inclusive.

Which purchases are sales?

Treat a purchase as a finalized sale only when:

Code
status === "confirmed"

pending is in-flight, and canceled / failed never took payment. Filter server-side with the status query parameter.

Which line items are products?

Line items have a type:

typeMeaningInclude in a product-sales export?
productA sellable catalogue itemYes
tipA gratuity lineNo
amountAn abstract amount paid toward a split/partial billNo

Discounts are not separate line items — they are a field on the product line (see below).

Prices, quantity, and VAT

Read these fields per line item:

FieldWhat it is
finalAmountCentsAuthoritative per-unit price, VAT-inclusive, after discount.
totalAmountCentsLine total = finalAmountCents × quantity. May be null/0 on some legacy purchases — if you need a guaranteed line total, compute finalAmountCents × quantity yourself.
appliedTotalDiscountAmountCentsDiscount on this line, a positive number, already subtracted from the amounts above. Gross before discount = totalAmountCents + appliedTotalDiscountAmountCents.
quantityWhole-unit count.
quantityCentsquantity × 100 — divide by 100 for fractional/weight-based items.
vatRateBasisPointsVAT rate in basis points; ÷ 100 for the percentage (1200 → 12%, 2500 → 25%).
vatAmountCentsVAT per unit (already contained in finalAmountCents).
totalVatAmountCentsVAT for the whole line = vatAmountCents × quantity.

Don't rely on pre_discount_value_cents or total_with_modifications_cents. The former no longer exists; the latter is rarely populated. finalAmountCents + appliedTotalDiscountAmountCents are the fields to build on.

Modifiers and bundles

Modifiers show up two ways:

  • Inline, in appliedModifications — an array like [{ title, priceAdjustmentCents, variantRef? }]. Discounts and vouchers appear here as negative priceAdjustmentCents. These entries do not carry an article number.
  • As child line items, when a variant/add-on maps to its own catalogue item. The child row points at its parent via parentLineItemId.

⚠️ Avoid double-counting. Because add-ons can appear as separate child lines, summing every line's total can over- or under-count a bundle depending on how the product is modelled. Reconcile your per-purchase line sum against the purchase amount as a check.

Matching a sale line to your own product catalogue

articleNo is a Karma-internal reference used for fiscal cash-register registration — despite the name it is not your SKU/PLU/article number, and it will not match your catalogue.

To link a sale line to your own product, use originItemId — the catalogue item the line was sold from. Join originItemId to the item, where your own external article number lives (populated from your inventory/POS setup). That join, not articleNo, is the stable key to your catalogue.

Refunds

Refunds are represented against the purchase. Refund amounts are stored as positive values (the magnitude refunded) — negate them for a ledger. A refund is valid once it is confirmed.

Timing: when is a sale final?

There is no single "finalized at" flag. In practice:

  • A purchase's payment is final at status === "confirmed".
  • Fee and settlement data can be written asynchronously after capture (minutes to a couple of hours later), so if you need fees, don't treat a just-confirmed purchase as complete for fee purposes.
  • Late corrections and refunds can arrive afterward.

A safe pattern is to only export purchases that have been settled for a few hours, and to re-poll on the update timestamp to catch late changes.
